decision: Use fetch wrapper instead of Hono RPC
alternatives: Hono RPC (type-safe but couples to backend)
rationale: Frontend must work with both TypeScript (Hono) and Python (FastAPI) backends. A simple fetch wrapper with Zod validation achieves type safety without backend coupling.

alternatives: generic admin-only — every project inherits the sidebar shell
archetype as a closed hard-typed enum — forces the least-bad fit
rationale: AI agents defaulted every product to an admin sidebar because the only reference slice was CRUD. Layer 0 archetype + focused/split shell presets + a *-list.tsx-gated CRUD contract + a governed custom escape hatch let an agent build non-admin UIs without regressing. Chosen via CED multi-model debate; all four traces converged on presets+escape.

decision: Use body-portaled fixed listboxes with a nested scroll lock
alternatives: body portal relying only on native overflow
body portal with viewport geometry and nested RemoveScroll
rationale: Dialog transforms break descendant fixed coordinates, while Radix modal scroll locks suppress native wheel and touch input on body portals. A no-isolation nested RemoveScroll composes with the active dialog lock and preserves native input without moving or clipping the panel.

decision: One error and session policy in the QueryClient caches, errors rendered inside the layout
alternatives: a fetch wrapper that redirects on 401
QueryCache and MutationCache onError plus defaultErrorComponent
rationale: Per-hook handling drifted (no hook handled 401) and a redirecting fetch wrapper cannot clear the query cache. The cache-level onError sees every query and mutation once, clears cached data from the lost session and returns to the same page after login; rendering errors per route keeps the menu and gives a retry that re-runs the loader without a reload. Loader prefetches ignore a CancelledError because React can hide a cached page mid-load and unsubscribe the only observer; the page refetches on mount.

decision: Suave as the default identity: one token block + one icon wrapper re-skin the app
alternatives: keep Aether (neutral black/white + Geist, indistinguishable from stock shadcn)
src/themes/<identity>.css files (blocked by INVARIANT #10: styles.css is the only CSS file)
identity block inside styles.css with semantic radius/shadow/density/motion utilities
rationale: Projects built from the skeleton all looked like default shadcn because the look lived in dark: overrides and rgba values inside components and the theme only varied --primary. Moving every visual value into one IDENTITY block (colors, fonts, radii, elevation, density, motion) and every icon import behind src/ui/icons.ts makes the look swappable per product, keeps shadcn token names so tweakcn/shadcn-create exports paste over it, and lets the design guard ban the generic tells (icon tiles, uppercase labels, gradients) instead of enforcing one aesthetic.

decision: The session check (authQueryOptions) runs without an AbortSignal and with networkMode 'always'
alternatives: catch CancelledError in the _authed beforeLoad and ask again
stop the pending screen from observing auth/me
drop the signal from the session query only
rationale: The _authed beforeLoad awaits the same ['auth','me'] fetch that the pending screen observes. When a query consumed its signal (or was paused offline), an observer unmounting mid-request cancels the fetch and the guard rejects with CancelledError, so a reload showed 'Algo salió mal' (30/50 reloads with a 500 ms auth/me, 0/50 after). Not reading the signal makes an unmount only stop retries; the api-client timeout still bounds the request. A retry in the guard would hide the race instead of removing it, and keeping the pending screen from reading the user would cost the layout its user menu.
